title: The Intelligent Interface: Sam Whitmore & Jason Yuan of New Computer
talk_summary: This is a design/UX keynote about multimodal 'intelligent interfaces' — sensing/thinking/reacting loops, pose detection to decide input modality, and speculative gesture/projection demos.

takeaways.technique: LLM-decided input modality from cheap sensor signals
takeaways.what_they_do: Feed lightweight signals (pose detection: near keyboard, facing screen) into an LLM reasoning step that decides whether to accept voice vs text input and how to respond, rather than hardcoding the mode.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're using an llm to actually make that choice as it as it goes to the response

takeaways.technique: Graceful escape hatch for probabilistic outputs
takeaways.what_they_do: When a probabilistic system mis-fires, provide a low-friction undo (flick away) rather than requiring explicit command-Z, so errors are cheap to recover from.
takeaways.evidence_quote: anytime you work with probabilistic materials you want to provide a graceful way out
